hints: Symmetrical about $x = 4$ means the area to the left of $4$ is the same as the area to the right, and $x = 3$ and $x = 5$ are the same distance from $4$ on opposite sides. Start with the area above $5$: $1 - \frac{20}{27}$.
The tail below $3$ is the mirror image of the tail above $5$, so it has the same area. Then $\text{P}(3 < X < 5) = \text{P}(X < 5) - \text{P}(X < 3)$.
walkthrough:
**Draw the picture in your head**

The curve is a mirror image about the vertical line $x = 4$. The points $x = 3$ and $x = 5$ are each exactly 1 unit away from $4$, one on each side. Because of the mirror symmetry, the area to the left of $3$ is the same as the area to the right of $5$.

**Find the area to the right of 5 (M1)**

All the area under a pdf is $1$. We are told the area to the left of $5$ is $\frac{20}{27}$, so the area to the right of $5$ is the rest:

$$\text{P}(X > 5) = 1 - \frac{20}{27} = \frac{27}{27} - \frac{20}{27} = \frac{7}{27}$$

This is the first expression the mark scheme looks for (M1).

**Use symmetry for the left tail**

By the mirror symmetry, the area to the left of $3$ equals the area to the right of $5$:

$$\text{P}(X < 3) = \text{P}(X > 5) = \frac{7}{27}$$

**Find the area between 3 and 5 (A1)**

The area to the left of $5$ includes the area to the left of $3$. To keep only the part between $3$ and $5$, take away the part to the left of $3$:

$$\text{P}(3 < X < 5) = \text{P}(X < 5) - \text{P}(X < 3) = \frac{20}{27} - \frac{7}{27} = \frac{13}{27}$$

Quick check by another route: the area from $4$ to $5$ is $\frac{20}{27} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{40}{54} - \frac{27}{54} = \frac{13}{54}$. Doubling it (for the matching piece between $3$ and $4$) gives $\frac{26}{54} = \frac{13}{27}$, the same.

**Final answer**

$\text{P}(3 < X < 5) = \mathbf{\dfrac{13}{27}}$ (which is $0.481$ as a decimal).
